question: What is the main goal when doing rehabilitation care for older adults?

options.A: Accelerating the normal aging process in the body
options.B: Curing all chronic illnesses present in the patient
options.C: Maximizing the patient's independence and function
options.D: Providing permanent custodial nursing home placement

explanation: You're doing great! Gerontological rehab is all about helping older adults do as much as they can for themselves, rather than just chasing a cure for old age. Keep it up!

question: Why should you as a nurse encourage older patients to do tasks themselves instead of doing everything for them?

options.A: To reduce the total number of nursing staff needed on duty
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge paperwork process
options.C: To comply with strict hospital punishment regulations
options.D: To prevent rapid physical deconditioning and loss of ability

explanation: Spot on! When older adults stop moving and doing things, their muscles weaken very fast. Encouraging self-care keeps them strong and mobile.

question: A complete health assessment for an older adult looks at their physical health plus what other key areas?

options.A: Only the financial savings of the patient
options.B: Past employment history from early adulthood
options.D: Genomic sequencing for rare inherited disorders

explanation: Brilliant! A good geriatric assessment looks at the whole person—their mental state, emotions, and family support, not just their physical sickness.

question: An older stroke patient says their biggest goal is to walk to the backyard garden to see flowers. How should you use this?

options.A: Ignore the statement because garden visits are not medical milestones
options.B: Tell the patient to pick a standard treadmill speed instead
options.C: Incorporate the garden walk into realistic, patient-centered goal setting
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they have outdoor desires

explanation: You've got this! When rehab goals matter personally to the patient, they feel much more motivated to work hard and get better.

question: What is the main idea behind restorative nursing care for elderly patients?

options.A: To replace physical therapy sessions entirely
options.B: To diagnose new chronic illnesses in older adults
options.C: To provide heavy sedation during painful medical procedures
options.D: To integrate rehabilitation principles into daily nursing routines

explanation: Exactly! Restorative nursing simply means weaving rehab into everyday actions like bathing, eating, and getting out of bed.

question: Why is it better to help an older patient sit in a chair for meals instead of keeping them flat in bed?

options.A: It saves the nursing staff time during meal distribution
options.B: It is a strict hospital rule with no clinical reasoning behind it
options.C: It completely cures chronic joint arthritis in the legs
options.D: It prevents muscle deconditioning and improves digestion and alertness

explanation: Well done! Sitting upright helps them swallow safely, digests food better, and keeps them awake and alert.

question: Which of these is a common home hazard that causes older adults to fall?

options.B: Low pile carpeting securely glued to the floor
options.C: Loose scatter rugs and cluttered pathways
options.D: Sturdy grab bars installed near the toilet

explanation: Correct! Loose rugs and messy walkways are classic traps that easily trip up older people. Good thing to watch out for in clinical practice!

question: Why is checking a patient's medications a key part of preventing falls?

options.A: Medications are the only known cause of falls in the elderly
options.B: Pharmacists require routine checks to maintain their licenses
options.C: Older adults always take too many vitamins instead of real food
options.D: Many common drugs cause dizziness, sedation, or balance issues

explanation: Spot on! Blood pressure pills and sleeping meds can make a patient dizzy or lightheaded, leading to accidental falls.

question: What common mental health challenge can block an older adult's progress during physical rehabilitation?
explanation: You're doing great! Depression drains a patient's drive and energy, making it tough for them to participate in rehab exercises.

question: How do daily routines and familiar activities help a patient with dementia during recovery?

options.A: They completely reverse brain cell death caused by Alzheimer's disease
options.B: They cure chronic sleep apnea permanently
options.C: They eliminate the need for any physical therapy exercises
options.D: They reduce confusion and help the patient feel secure enough to participate

explanation: Exactly right! Predictable routines calm anxiety and make confused patients feel safe enough to cooperate with care.

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and increased muscle weakness
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic stroke symptoms
options.D: Rapid muscle growth and increased strength

explanation: Brilliant! Without good food and protein, the body simply doesn't have the fuel to repair tissues or build strength.

question: What is the best way to help an older, weak patient who has a very poor appetite?

options.A: Providing nutrient-dense small meals and a pleasant dining setting
options.B: Withdrawing all food until the patient requests a heavy meal
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.D: Forcing large meals three times a day regardless of complaints

explanation: Well done! Small, rich portions are much easier for a weak patient to finish without feeling overwhelmed.

question: Which healthcare worker usually acts as the central link for the team because they spend the most time at the bedside?
explanation: Spot on! Because nurses are always close to the patient, they are in the best position to spot changes and coordinate care.

question: Why is good communication so important when an older patient moves from the rehab center back home?

options.A: It prevents confusion and ensures therapy strategies are continued safely
options.B: It is only done to satisfy mandatory government billing forms
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never need medical care again
options.D: It allows the physical therapist to move into the patient's house

explanation: You nailed it! Smooth handover notes and clear instructions ensure family members know how to keep caring for the patient safely at home.
